title: Charlie Parker pawns a roommate's suit and takes two dollars
summary: Two anecdotes show Parker's persuasive logic: the pawned suit and gently reaching into Malachi's pocket.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I'm trying to think... There was just so many funny things happened that I'm reminded of. I think it was in Cleveland, Ohio, where I got the first inkling of Charlie Parker, some of his erratic behavior. Because he had a room with someone in the band who came into Billy Eckstine's room one day... We were all sitting in Billy Eckstine's room. He came in, and he was mad as hell. Everybody wanted to know what was wrong, and he said that he and Bird were rooming together, and he woke up one morning, and Bird had been out and was just coming back in... And I don't remember who this was, but he asked Bird where he'd been, and Bird told him, he said, "I've been out. Oh, incidentally, I pawned your suit.

I've got the ticket. I'll get it back." So this guy is as mad as he can be, and he's raising all this fuss. And Charlie Parker said, "Man, if you think it's that bad, here, you take the ticket and you get it. I told you I'll get it out for you when I get some money. You're not going to wear the suit. We wear our uniforms on the job." And this is kind of the rationale sometimes that Charlie Parker would have.

I remember him coming to me one time, asking me to let him have two dollars. And I said, "I don't have two dollars." He said, "Oh sure, you do. Sure you have two dollars, man. Don't give me that." I said, "No, Charlie, I don't have it." So then, he proceeded to just gently run his hand in my pocket. I said, "Man, don't run your hand in my pocket." He says, "Why not?" "I don't want you to." He said, "That's not the reason. The reason is because you do have two dollars." I said, "Well, okay, I got two dollars, but I have things to do with it, and I don't have two dollars to give to you." He said, "Why didn't you tell me that in the first place? Don't lie to me. We're friends." And this was the kind of thing that he could put you on the defense where you weren't even aware of it!
